newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish share index at new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Turkish share index at new all-time high.

text.p: The Turkish stock market index rose to another all-time high on Friday, bringing gains in the week to a total 7.15 percent, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 index closed at 76,694.86, up 1.9 percent from the previous closing high on Thursday. Trading volume slipped to 16.5 trillion lira ($178,416) from 24.5 trillion lira.

Renewed market confidence has driven the index up nearly 20 percent since mid-September, as dealers put aside concerns about the coalition government of Islamist premier Necmettin Erbakan and focus more on corporate earnings, analysts said.
They said technical indicators point to a continuation of the rally.
"The sideways canal has been breached by today's closing in the weekly graphics. That sets the target of the index at 85,000," said Zehra Dislioglu, Garanti Yatirim Bank analyst.
"It is likely for the index to meet a pull-back resistance at 77,200-77,300, but the weekly signs are so good that it could breach that level easily," she added.
Brokers said the rally remained limited to selected stocks and more broad-based gains would be necessary to sustain the uptrend next week.
"It will only be possible for the index to go up to 78,000 and 80,000 levels if demand is spread over the private sector shares," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank Securities. ($1=92,480 lira)
